title: Why our SaaS growth stalls: three coupled feedback loops
caption: Causal loop model of the retention/growth system. Polarity per link; R/B set by sign-product of each closed cycle.

variables.label: Active Users
variables.description: Customers actively using the product this month.

variables.label: Referrals
variables.description: Word-of-mouth invitations generated by satisfied users.

variables.label: Support Response Time
variables.description: Median hours to first reply on a ticket.

variables.label: Churn Rate
variables.description: Share of users cancelling each month.

variables.label: Revenue Pressure
variables.description: Board pressure to cut cost when revenue softens.

variables.label: Support Investment
variables.description: Headcount and tooling funding for the support org.

links.note: More happy users send more invites.
Onboarding lag before a signup becomes active.
Slow support frustrates users into leaving.
More support capacity lowers response time.

loops.label: Word-of-mouth growth engine
loops.narrative: Active users drive referrals, referrals drive signups, signups become active users. All links positive (zero negatives, even) so the loop is reinforcing: growth feeds growth.

loops.label: Capacity ceiling
loops.narrative: Growth raises support load and response time, slow support raises churn, churn cuts active users. Exactly one negative link (churn to active users), so the loop is balancing: scale throttles itself.

loops.label: Austerity death spiral
loops.narrative: Churn raises revenue pressure, which cuts support investment, which raises response time, which raises churn. Two negative links (even), so the loop is reinforcing decline once it tips.

semantic_description.level_1_elemental: A causal loop diagram with eight variables (Active Users, Referrals, New Signups, Support Load, Support Response Time, Churn Rate, Revenue Pressure, Support Investment) connected by ten signed arrows; six links are positive and four are negative, with two arrows marked as delayed.
semantic_description.level_2_statistical: Three closed feedback loops are declared: one reinforcing growth loop (R1, three positive links), one balancing capacity loop (B1, one negative link among four), and one reinforcing decline loop (R2, two negative links among four). Active Users participates in both R1 and B1; Response Time and Churn are the shared variables coupling B1 to R2.
semantic_description.level_3_perceptual: Active Users sits at the hub where the growth engine and the capacity ceiling meet, so the loop that dominates determines whether the system expands or stalls. Churn and Response Time form a second coupling point feeding the austerity spiral, meaning a revenue scare can convert a self-limiting system into a self-accelerating decline.
semantic_description.level_4_contextual: The leverage point is Support Investment: protecting it during a revenue scare breaks R2 and keeps the system in the gentler balancing regime of B1 rather than the reinforcing collapse of R2.
semantic_description.short_alt: CLD of SaaS retention: a reinforcing growth loop and a balancing capacity loop meet at Active Users; an austerity loop couples churn to support.
